findings.claim: The bound added for -2 F1 is stated and tested as a Linux constant, but it is not one. Linux defines MAX_ARG_STRLEN as 32 * PAGE_SIZE. That is 128 KiB only with 4 KiB pages. It is 512 KiB with 16 KiB pages (for example Asahi arm64) and 2 MiB with 64 KiB pages (for example some aarch64 and ppc64le distribution kernels). On such a kernel, test (k) passes 9,000 identifiers joined into about 162 KB. awk starts, prints 9,000 'no' lines and exits 0, so the 'past the bound' case fails, although the only guard is runtime.GOOS == "linux". The same holds where sh runs awk as a busybox applet without exec. The header of evidence.sh (line 51) and PROVENANCE.md say '128 KiB on Linux', and the test pins that figure as a needle. These are the documented bound that T4w's adapter relies on, and on those systems they are wrong. The answers stay correct (the failure is the safe one), so the defect is a false test failure and an inaccurate deployed claim, not a wrong answer. This reasoning comes from the kernel definition as recalled, not from source read here.

The known-error lint for -5 F5, TestEvidenceStore_ReadsEveryEnvironmentValueAsAString, finds reads only with the regex ENVIRON\["[^"]*"\]. That is a literal double-quoted subscript with no blanks inside the brackets. It also needs exactly one space and "" right after the read. A later read written as ENVIRON[name], ENVIRON[ "X" ] or ENVIRON["X"]"" is either not found at all or fails for spacing alone. The len(reads) == 0 guard fires only when no read is found at all, so a second read that is numeric-compared goes unnoticed while the existing one still matches. The class the lint exists to catch (an environment value compared as a number) can come back through a read the lint cannot see.
